idiom_name: interface satisfaction + function values registered with a framework (net/http Handler)
implementation_notes: Go replaces the abstract framework class with an interface plus function values: implementing ServeHTTP - or passing a func(w, r) where a Handler is expected - is the entire extension contract, while net/http's Server owns the listen-accept-dispatch loop that invokes it. Passing an explicit interface instead of a bare func is still the right form when the hook needs configuration or shared state, but no framework base class has to be written by hand and registration is a single call.
pitfalls: Handlers run on many goroutines at once: state captured in a handler struct must be immutable or synchronised, and per-request state belongs in locals.
The server recovers panics raised inside ServeHTTP, logs a stack trace and aborts the request - a bug therefore fails far from where it was caused unless errors are returned explicitly.
